meta.description: Alternate tagging taxonomy organized around the SF-36v2 Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) instrument. Eight top-level themes (h3) correspond to the eight SF-36v2 scales; each is annotated with its component summary (PCS = Physical Component Summary; MCS = Mental Component Summary; GH belongs to both). Subthemes (h4) map to the canonical item facets within each scale, framed so taggers can apply them to free-form patient language (interview transcripts, social-corpus fragments) rather than to structured questionnaire responses. Sentiment scale carries forward from codebook.json @ 2.0 unchanged. Emotions are NOT inlined here — the single source of truth is src/lib/content/emotions/plutchik.ts (exports PLUTCHIK_EMOTIONS, PLUTCHIK_DYADS, ALL_EMOTION_IDS); the live codebook.json duplicates that list and we are not propagating the duplication. Cluster arrays are intentionally empty — populate the same way as the live codebook (cluster declares parent_theme + parent_subtheme).
changelog: sf36v2-1.0 — initial SF-36v2 mirror of the live codebook. Themes structure replaced; meta notes and sentiment_scale preserved. Emotion taxonomy intentionally omitted in favor of content/emotions/plutchik.ts as the single source of truth. Subthemes derived from the SF-36v2 item content of each scale (e.g. PF's vigorous/moderate/lifting/climbing/walking/self-care; MH's anxiety/depression/calm/positive-affect).
notes: A segment may carry a theme with no subtheme (general use) or with one or more subthemes.
A subtheme may only be applied if its parent theme is also applied.
Each theme declares its SF-36v2 `component` (PCS, MCS, or both) so component-level rollups stay derivable without re-tagging.
Themes are not mutually exclusive — a single fragment about pain interfering with work and mood can carry BP, RP, and MH.

Cluster tags are recorded per-instance in keyword_tags.json with absolute char spans. A cluster's parent_theme/parent_subtheme is a default home for UI nesting — it does NOT auto-tag the segment with those parents when a span is tagged to the cluster.
Emotions follow the Plutchik model. Source of truth: src/lib/content/emotions/plutchik.ts. Tagging code that needs the valid id set should import ALL_EMOTION_IDS from there (not from this file).

This codebook is content-only; downstream consumers (proposer scripts, exec-summary, drawers) currently target codebook.json. To use this file, point loaders at codebook.sf36v2.json or run a migration.

instrument_reference.name: SF-36v2 Health Survey
instrument_reference.note: Scale names and item content follow Ware et al. (2007), SF-36v2 Health Survey: Administration Guide. This codebook uses the SF-36v2 scales as a tagging vocabulary; it is not a scoring or psychometric instrument.

themes.label: Physical Functioning
themes.description: Extent to which health limits physical activities — from vigorous exertion through basic self-care. Applies whenever a participant describes what their body can or can't do.

subthemes.label: Vigorous Activities
subthemes.description: Limitations in running, lifting heavy objects, strenuous sports, or other high-exertion activity.

subthemes.label: Moderate Activities
subthemes.description: Limitations in moving a table, vacuuming, bowling, golfing, or similar moderate-effort activity.

subthemes.label: Lifting & Carrying
subthemes.description: Difficulty lifting or carrying groceries and similar everyday loads.

subthemes.label: Climbing Stairs
subthemes.description: Difficulty climbing one or several flights of stairs.

subthemes.label: Bending, Kneeling, Stooping
subthemes.description: Difficulty bending, kneeling, or stooping.

subthemes.label: Walking
subthemes.description: Limitations walking — more than a mile, several blocks, or even one block.

subthemes.label: Bathing & Dressing
subthemes.description: Difficulty with bathing, dressing, and other basic self-care.

subthemes.label: Mobility Aids & Adaptations
subthemes.description: Use of canes, walkers, wheelchairs, grab bars, or other aids; home or environment adaptations made to compensate for physical limits. Not an SF-36 item, but commonly volunteered when PF limits are discussed in free text.

themes.label: Role-Physical
themes.description: Extent to which physical health interferes with work and other regular daily activities — productivity lost, effort required, kinds of tasks given up.

subthemes.label: Cut Down Time
subthemes.description: Reducing the amount of time spent on work or other activities because of physical health.

subthemes.label: Accomplished Less
subthemes.description: Getting less done than wanted as a result of physical health.

subthemes.label: Limited in Kind of Work
subthemes.description: Restricted in the kind of work or activities that can be done due to physical health (e.g. switching roles, dropping tasks).

subthemes.label: Difficulty Performing
subthemes.description: Work or activities take extra effort, more time, or workarounds to complete due to physical health.

subthemes.label: Career & Income Impact
subthemes.description: Job loss, reduced hours, missed promotions, disability leave, or income loss attributed to physical health. Not an SF-36 item, but commonly volunteered around RP content in free text.

themes.label: Bodily Pain
themes.description: Intensity of pain and the extent to which pain interferes with normal work and daily activity.

subthemes.label: Pain Intensity
subthemes.description: How much bodily pain the participant has experienced — including severity, frequency, and pain that is described as constant or chronic.

subthemes.label: Pain Interference
subthemes.description: How much pain interferes with normal work, household tasks, hobbies, or daily activities — inside and outside the home.

subthemes.label: Pain Location & Quality
subthemes.description: Where the pain is felt (back, joints, head, abdominal, neuropathic, etc.) and how it is described (sharp, burning, throbbing, aching). Not a separate SF-36 item, but a common qualitative facet of BP language.

subthemes.label: Pain Management
subthemes.description: Strategies and treatments used to manage pain — medications, procedures, physical therapy, alternative approaches — and how well they work.

themes.label: General Health
themes.description: Personal evaluation of overall health — self-rating, comparison to others, expectations about the future, and beliefs about one's own susceptibility to illness.

subthemes.label: Health Self-Rating
subthemes.description: How the participant rates their health overall (excellent / very good / good / fair / poor) and the language they use to summarize it in their own words.

subthemes.label: Illness Susceptibility
subthemes.description: Belief that they get sick more easily than other people, or claims that they are as healthy as anybody they know.

subthemes.label: Health Outlook
subthemes.description: Expectation that health will get worse, stay the same, or improve over time.

subthemes.label: Health Comparison
subthemes.description: Comparison of current health to a year ago, to peers, or to a prior baseline.

themes.label: Vitality
themes.description: Energy level and fatigue — feeling full of life and pep at one end, worn out and tired at the other.

subthemes.label: Full of Life
subthemes.description: Feeling lively, vital, full of life — the positive pole of the vitality scale.

subthemes.label: Energy
subthemes.description: Having a lot of energy; feeling able to do what one wants to do.

subthemes.label: Worn Out
subthemes.description: Feeling worn out, drained, depleted — beyond ordinary tiredness.

subthemes.label: Tired
subthemes.description: Feeling tired, sluggish, low-energy in a way the participant attributes to health or treatment.

themes.label: Social Functioning
themes.description: Extent to which physical or emotional health interferes with normal social activities with family, friends, neighbors, or groups.

subthemes.label: Extent of Interference
subthemes.description: How much physical or emotional problems have interfered with normal social activities with family, friends, neighbors, or groups (not at all → extremely).

subthemes.label: Frequency of Interference
subthemes.description: How much of the time physical or emotional health has interfered with social activities (none of the time → all of the time).

subthemes.label: Relationship Strain
subthemes.description: Strain on relationships with partners, family, friends, or caregivers attributed to health. Common qualitative facet of SF language in interviews.

subthemes.label: Isolation & Withdrawal
subthemes.description: Withdrawing from social events, declining invitations, or feeling isolated as a consequence of health.

themes.label: Role-Emotional
themes.description: Extent to which emotional problems (e.g. feeling depressed or anxious) interfere with work and other regular daily activities.

subthemes.label: Cut Down Time (Emotional)
subthemes.description: Reducing the amount of time spent on work or other activities because of emotional problems.

subthemes.label: Accomplished Less (Emotional)
subthemes.description: Getting less done than wanted as a result of emotional problems.

subthemes.label: Did Work Less Carefully
subthemes.description: Doing work or activities less carefully than usual because of emotional problems.

themes.label: Mental Health
themes.description: Psychological distress and well-being — anxiety, depression, behavioral and emotional control, and general positive affect.

subthemes.label: Anxiety & Nervousness
subthemes.description: Feeling very nervous, on edge, or anxious.

subthemes.label: Depression & Low Mood
subthemes.description: Feeling so down in the dumps that nothing could cheer one up; feeling downhearted, depressed, or hopeless.

subthemes.label: Calm & Peaceful
subthemes.description: Feeling calm and peaceful — the positive pole of the affect-balance content.

subthemes.label: Happiness
subthemes.description: Being a happy person — general positive emotional tone over the recall period.

subthemes.label: Emotional Control
subthemes.description: Sense of being in control of (or losing control of) one's emotions or behavior; mood swings; reactivity.
